newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds endure supply, Lilco, Atels up.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds endure supply, Lilco, Atels up.

text.p: U.S. investment and junk corporate bond spreads weathered a resurgence in supply on Wednesday, while secondary markets were focused on gains in Long Island Lighting Co and American Telecasting debt, dealers across both markets said.

High-yield secondary trade was marked by a surge in wireless cable concerns following news regional operator BellSouth Corp would acquire operations and assets in nine Southern markets from American Telecasting Inc.
Further, talk of an alliance by Cable & Wireless Plc and Sprint Corp proved positive for Sprint related debt.

Atel zero coupon bonds due 2005 traded as high as 37 after the news, traders said, up from Tuesday's closing bid in the low 20s. The deal, considered by analysts a confirmation on the value of spectrum assets of wireless cables, also boosted debt of similar companies such as CAI Wireless Systems Inc and People's Choice TV Corp.
The industry was upended last December when Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp suspended an agreement to develop a wireless network with CAI.
"The pendulum has swung the other way," said Salomon Brothers high-yield cable analyst Stevyn Schutzman.
Atel zeros closed off their highs at 32 bid, 33-1/2 offer.

High-yield issuance was active. Deals included: $200 million 10-7/8 percent senior subordinated notes due 2004 from Anacomp Inc priced to yield 11-1/4 percent; $125 million 10-1/4 percent 10-year senior subordinated notes from Key Plastics Inc at par; $100 million 11 percent 10-year senior subordinated notes from STC Broadcasting Inc at par; $100 million 11 percent 10-year senior subordinated notes from EV International Inc at par; and $125 million 9-5/8 percent 10-year senior subordinated notes from Borg-Warner Security Corp priced at a discount to yield 300 basis points over.
Not all deals were fortunate, however. Blue Chip Casino's planned $80 million seven-year senior secured deal was postponed for the second time, sources said.
Michigan City, Indiana-based Blue Chip Casinos did not return telephone calls.

Turning to investment grades, Long Island Lighting Co debenture spreads tightened more than 15 basis points on the day after news the Long Island Power Authority will acquire "spongy" distribution and regulatory assets and assume or refinance $3.6 billion in stranded costs, traders said.
The debt is now a full 100 basis points tighter than quotes prior December's announcement of the planned merger between Long Island Lighting Co and Brooklyn Union Gas Co, traders added.
Lilco's nine percent debt was quoted at 117 bid.

Other secondary trade was quiet with investors still playing coy with long U.S. Treasuries looming around seven percent and ahead of a possible short-term interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve next week, dealers said. Still, spreads were little changed and new issues were said to garner "decent" demand.

Issues included $200 million 10-year 7-1/2 percent notes from Fletcher Challenge Capital Canada Inc priced to yield 77 basis points over Treasuries. Another $150 million 7-7/8 percent 20-year bonds from Fletcher were priced to yield 87 basis points over.

Also, Chrysler Financial Corp issued $300 million 6.95 percent five-year notes to yield 40 basis points over and TCI Communications Financing IV issued $200 million worth of 40-year trust preferred securities with a 9.72 percent coupon (dividend) at par.
